docs.title: CRM → Ops move-in handoff
docs.text: A small n8n automation for a co-living operator. When Sales closes a booking in LeadSquared, Ops hears about it within seconds (WhatsApp and email), with the date the room has to be ready. Every Monday morning there's a summary of what's coming up and what's overdue.

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
An allotment tracker had 65 residents stuck before move-in: 29 marked Pending Move In and 36 marked Not Ready. All 35 who had a move-in date were already past it, by 26 to 138 days.

The cause wasn't slow cleaning. It was the handoff:

  • Ops learns a room needs turning only when the resident arrives. Nothing tells them when Sales closes the deal.
  • Friday-evening requests wait until Monday.

The process fix proposed to the Heads of Sales and Ops was:

  1. Closed Won creates an Ops task the same day.
  2. Ops marks the room Ready 2 working days before move-in (by Friday noon for Saturday-to-Monday move-ins).
  3. A 10-minute review every Monday of the next two weeks.

This workflow makes that process run without anyone having to remember it.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. A lead reaches Closed Won in LeadSquared, and LeadSquared calls the workflow.
  2. The workflow checks what Ops needs (bed, move-in date, gender, sales owner, phone) and flags anything missing in plain words.
  3. It works out Ready-by, the time the room must be ready (rules).
  4. It adds the task to the Ops Queue Google Sheet, or updates it if the same lead comes in again.
  5. It alerts that wing's Ops contact on WhatsApp and by email.
  6. Every Monday at 09:00 IST, everyone listed gets the move-in review.

Ops closes the loop in the Sheet by changing Status: Pending Move In → Ready → Moved In. There's no new app to learn.

docs.title: What Ops receives
docs.text:
New move-in: Priya S (Girls), Wing A A-204 R1 bed 2. Move-in Tue 3 Nov, room Ready by Fri 30 Oct 18:00. Sales: Rohit K.

When something is missing, the alert says so first:

⚠ Missing: move-in date, sales owner; No date – chase Sales. New move-in: Aman R (Boys), Wing B B-110 R2 bed 1. Move-in date not set. Sales: ?.

Monday 09:00:

Move-in review – Mon 2 Nov
Move-ins next 14 days: 1
Overdue (not Ready): 1
No date – chase Sales: 1
Waiting longest:
- Priya S (Wing A), 4 days
- Aman R (Wing B), 4 days
Full list: <sheet link>

docs.title: The flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  LSQ[LeadSquared<br/>lead updated] -->|webhook + secret| S[Read Settings]
  S --> E[Read existing task]
  E --> B{Build Ops task<br/>Closed Won?}
  B -->|no| X[stop]
  B -->|yes| Q[Ops Queue sheet<br/>add or update]
  Q --> C{Ops contact?}
  C -->|yes| W[WhatsApp alert]
  C -->|yes| G[Email alert]
  M[Monday 09:00] --> R[Read Ops Queue] --> RS[Read Settings] --> SUM[Build summary] --> W2[WhatsApp + email to each contact]

All the business rules live in one file, handoff.js. build.js copies it into the workflow's Code nodes, so the rules that are tested are the same ones that run.

docs.title: Ready-by rule
docs.text:
Working days are Monday to Friday. Public holidays are ignored for now.

Move-in day Room ready by If the request arrives after that Tue previous Fri 18:00 Already late Wed Mon 18:00 Already late Thu Tue 18:00 Already late Fri Wed 18:00 Already late Sat / Sun / Mon previous Fri 12:00 Saturday 12:00 slot (Late request → Saturday slot); if that has passed too, Already late

All times are India time (IST), computed explicitly. n8n's code runner keeps time in UTC even when the server is set to IST, so the code never relies on the server clock's timezone.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
A task is always written, even when something is wrong, and the problem is spelled out in the Flags column and the alert:

Flag Meaning Missing: move-in date, sales owner Required fields Sales didn't fill in at Closed Won No date – chase Sales No usable move-in date, so no Ready-by is possible Already late The request arrived after the room should already have been ready Late request → Saturday slot Arrived after Friday noon for a Sat/Sun/Mon move-in No Ops contact for wing B Nobody in Settings to alert, so the row is written without a message

Impossible dates (like 31/2) are treated as missing rather than quietly rolled over to another day. Slash dates are read day-first (Indian format).

docs.title: When the same lead comes in again
docs.text:
The workflow matches on the LeadSquared lead ID.

  • It updates the row and sends an alert starting with Updated:.
  • Ops' Status is never overwritten. A room marked Ready stays Ready.
  • Waiting time counts from the first arrival.
  • Lateness is judged from when Ops first heard about that move-in date. If Sales fixes a phone number on Friday afternoon, an on-time Monday move-in doesn't turn "late".

docs.title: Monday summary
docs.text:
• Who it covers: only open tasks (Pending Move In or Not Ready).
  • What it counts: move-ins in the next 14 days, overdue rooms (Ready-by passed), and tasks with no date.
  • Who's at the top: the three tasks waiting longest.

It goes to every Ops contact listed in Settings, as the agenda for the Monday review.

docs.title: What's real and what's sample
docs.text:
• Real: the workflow, the rules and their tests, and the secret-protected webhook.
  • Sample:
  • Every lead is invented. send-test.sh posts a LeadSquared-shaped lead.
  • The LeadSquared field names (ProspectID, mx_Wing, mx_Move_in_Date, ...) are an assumption. To go live, capture one real webhook payload and change fromLsq() in handoff.js. It's the only place that knows those names.
  • WhatsApp uses Meta's free test number. Meta currently refuses sends until the account has billing set up, so email carries the demo; each WhatsApp step is set to continue on error. Settings has an Email column; a contact needs a WhatsApp number or an email. In production it would go through a WhatsApp provider such as WATI (n8n-nodes-wati, Send Template Message) with an approved message template.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: File What handoff.js All rules: field mapping, Ready-by, flags, alert text, Monday summary handoff.test.js Fixed-date checks for every rule (node handoff.test.js) build.js Builds workflow.json with handoff.js inlined into the Code nodes workflow.json Import into n8n (no credentials inside) payloads/, send-test.sh Sample LeadSquared leads and the script that sends them

docs.title: Set it up
docs.text: You need Docker and Node 18+. Node is only used for the tests and build.js; n8n itself runs in Docker.

docs.title: 1. Run n8n locally
docs.text:
From the repo folder:

docker run -d --name n8n -p 5678:5678 -e GENERIC_TIMEZONE=Asia/Kolkata -e TZ=Asia/Kolkata -v n8n_data:/home/node/.n8n -v "$PWD:/files" docker.n8n.io/n8nio/n8n

Open http://localhost:5678 and create your login.

docs.title: 2. Google Sheet
docs.text:
Create a Sheet with two tabs.

Ops Queue: row 1 headers, in this order:

Received at, LSQ Lead ID, Tenant, Phone, Gender, Wing, Flat, Room, Bed, Room Category, Move-in date, Ready-by, Sales owner, Status, Flags
  • Give Status a dropdown: Pending Move In, Not Ready, Ready, Moved In - Permanent, Moved In - Temp.
  • Format Received at, Move-in date and Ready-by as plain text (Format → Number → Plain text). Otherwise dates that Ops retypes won't count in the Monday summary.

Settings: headers Role, Wing, Name, WhatsApp, Email:

Role Wing Name WhatsApp Email Trigger stage Closed Won Wing Ops A name number email Wing Ops B name number email Ops Head name number email
  • Format the WhatsApp column as plain text, and write numbers with the country code, e.g. 919800000001.
  • Ops Head is the fallback when a wing has no contact.
  • Trigger stage is the LeadSquared stage that creates a task.

docs.title: 3. Credentials in n8n
docs.text:
• Google Sheets OAuth2 and Gmail OAuth2 (one OAuth client covers both; enable the Sheets, Drive and Gmail APIs):
  • In Google Cloud, create an OAuth client with redirect URI http://localhost:5678/rest/oauth2-credential/callback.
  • Add the credential in n8n and sign in.
  • WhatsApp:
  • On developers.facebook.com, create an app and add WhatsApp.
  • On API Setup, add and verify your phone as a recipient. Copy the Phone number ID, the WhatsApp Business Account ID and the access token into an n8n WhatsApp API credential.
  • Send "hi" from your phone to the test number. Plain-text messages only work within 24 hours of a message from your side.
  • Webhook secret:
  • Create a Header Auth credential named LeadSquared webhook secret, with header name X-Handoff-Secret and a long random value.
  • Copy .env.example to .env and put the same value in it.

docs.title: 4. Build, import, publish
docs.text:
SHEET_ID=<sheet id> WA_PHONE_ID=<phone number id> node build.js

docker exec n8n n8n import:workflow --input=/files/workflow.json && docker exec n8n n8n publish:workflow --id=ulOpsHandoff0001 && docker restart n8n

Open the workflow and pick your credentials on the webhook node, every Google Sheets node and both WhatsApp nodes. Then publish. Re-importing resets the credential picks, so pick them again after every rebuild.

docs.title: 5. Try it
docs.text:
./send-test.sh payloads/closed-won.json
Payload What should happen closed-won.json New row in Ops Queue, WhatsApp to Wing A's contact same file again Still one row; the alert starts Updated: missing-fields.json Row with Flags Missing: move-in date, sales owner; No date – chase Sales, alert starts ⚠ closed-lost.json Nothing: not Closed Won

To see the Monday summary now, open Monday 09:00 in the editor and click Execute workflow.

To run the rule tests: node handoff.test.js should print handoff ok.

docs.title: Going live with LeadSquared
docs.text:
Route 1: webhook (recommended).

  1. In LeadSquared, go to My Profile → Settings → API and Webhooks → Webhooks and create one webhook on Lead update.
  2. Point it at the production webhook URL and add the custom header X-Handoff-Secret.
  3. Lead update should also fire on stage changes. Confirm this with one real payload; if it doesn't, use Lead stage change instead.
  4. Don't subscribe to both events. One Closed Won could fire both at the same moment and create a duplicate row.
  5. n8n must be reachable from the internet: n8n Cloud, or a tunnel.

Route 2: polling, if webhooks aren't available.

  1. Enable the two greyed-out nodes.
  2. Add a Custom Auth credential with the headers x-LSQ-AccessKey and x-LSQ-SecretKey, and set your account's API host.
  3. Map the response to the same fields before Build Ops task.

Production WhatsApp: swap the WhatsApp nodes for your provider's node (for WATI, n8n-nodes-wati → Send Template Message) with an approved utility template.

Before going live: capture one real LeadSquared payload and adjust fromLsq() in handoff.js to the real field names. Check the date format too: if LeadSquared sends dates in UTC, a midnight-IST date would read one day early.
